Six warning signs your vent is clogged

One sign is a nuisance. Two or more usually mean the vent run is packed with lint and your dryer is straining on every load.

What a clogged vent actually looks like

This is the inside of a vent that has gone years without a cleaning: lint packed wall to wall until only a pinhole of airway is left. Hot, moist air hits that wall of lint and bounces straight back into your laundry room — which is why the signs below show up together. A full-run cleaning clears the whole duct, not just the trap.

1. Clothes take two cycles

Loads that used to dry in one cycle now come out damp — the classic sign that moist air has nowhere to go.

2. The laundry room feels hot and humid

Heat and moisture that should exit outside are backing up into the room instead.

3. A burning or musty smell

A hot, scorched smell during a cycle — or a musty odor on finished clothes — means lint and trapped moisture are building up.

4. The dryer is hot to the touch

When the top or sides of the dryer feel unusually hot, the machine is overheating because it cannot exhaust properly.

5. Lint around the door or outside cap

Extra lint on clothes, around the door seal, or piling up at the exterior vent flap points to a blocked run.

6. The outside flap barely opens

While the dryer runs, the exterior vent flap should open with strong airflow. A weak trickle means a clog.

Blocked vs. breathing

On the left, a mat of lint chokes the duct — air bounces back, heat builds up, and drying times double. On the right, a cleaned run lets hot, moist air leave the house the way the dryer was designed to work. That difference is what a cleaning restores, and we check airflow so you can feel it.

  • Shorter, single-cycle drying
  • Less strain and heat on the dryer
  • Lower energy wasted on repeat cycles
  • Lint — the fuel for dryer fires — removed from the run

How the cleaning works

1

Inspect and test

We check the dryer connection, the vent route, and the outside cap, and note the starting airflow.

2

Brush the full run

A rotary brush works through the entire vent line — not just the trap — loosening packed lint from the walls of the duct.

3

Vacuum it all out

Loosened lint is vacuumed out of the run and collected, so it leaves with us instead of settling back inside.

4

Reconnect and retest

We reconnect the dryer, confirm the outside flap opens freely, and retest airflow. We guarantee clean airflow with every cleaning.

Finished at the outside wall

A vent run is only clean when air moves freely at the exterior cap, so every job ends outside: the cap and flap are cleared, the brush passes the full length of the run, and we confirm strong airflow where the vent exits your home. If the run turns out to be crushed, disconnected, or routed in a way that will just clog again, we will show you — our related services cover repairs, rerouting, covers, and booster fans.

Frequently asked questions

How much does dryer vent cleaning cost?

A standard residential cleaning is $149 for first-floor laundry and $249 for second-floor laundry. Condos, HOAs, and multi-unit properties get per-unit pricing for full-building service days — call 954-931-7997 or send the quote form below for a building quote.

How long does a cleaning take?

Most standard home vents take about an hour, depending on the length of the run and how packed it is. Long, roof-exit, or heavily clogged runs can take a bit longer.

How often should a dryer vent be cleaned?

Once a year is the standard recommendation for most households. Large families, pet hair, and long vent runs may need it more often. Our Annual Cleaning Plan handles the scheduling for you.

Will cleaning really make my dryer dry faster?

If slow drying is caused by a clogged vent — the most common cause — yes. Restoring airflow lets moist air escape, so loads dry in one cycle again. If we find the problem is the dryer itself, we will tell you honestly.

What areas do you serve?

Coral Springs, Sunrise, Plantation, and Fort Lauderdale, plus nearby Broward County neighborhoods. If you are just outside those areas, call or text 954-931-7997 and ask — we will tell you straight away if we can get to you.

What are your hours?

Monday to Saturday, 8am to 5pm. Call or text 954-931-7997, or email Cleanoutvents@gmail.com any time and we will reply during hours.

Do I need to do anything before you arrive?

Just make sure we can reach the back of the dryer and the outside vent cap. Running one empty warm cycle before we arrive can help us feel the starting airflow, but it is optional.

Still damp after a full cycle? It’s not your dryer. It’s your vent.

Before you shop for a new dryer, check the vent. A dryer with a clogged vent tumbles and heats just fine — it just cannot push the damp air out of the house. The moisture stays trapped with your clothes, so you run a second cycle, and a third, for a machine that was never the problem.

Call 954-931-7997 Text us Get a quote
Offer on this page: Mention this page when you book and get a free airflow test before and after your cleaning, so you can see the difference in numbers — not just take our word for it.

Try this 2-minute check first

  • Feel the outside cap while the dryer runs on heat. Weak or no warm air coming out means the run is blocked.
  • Check the flap. The exterior flap should lift and stay open with strong airflow. Barely moving means a clog.
  • Notice the room. A hot, steamy laundry room during a cycle means exhaust is backing up indoors.
  • Empty the lint trap and retry. If drying is still slow with a clean trap, the problem is deeper in the vent run.

A full cleaning clears the entire run for $149 on the first floor or $249 on the second floor — usually far less than a repair call or a replacement dryer you do not need. We guarantee clean airflow with every cleaning.

The most flammable thing in your house is hiding in your dryer vent.

Lint is made to catch — it is the same material people use as a fire starter. Every load sheds a little more of it past the trap and into the vent run, where it packs against warm duct walls, load after load, year after year. A professional cleaning removes that fuel from the full run.

Source: U.S. Fire Administration, “Clothes dryer fires in residential buildings.” Figures are national estimates reported by USFA.

How a fire risk quietly builds up

It rarely starts with a spark. It starts with a hose that slipped off behind the dryer, or a vent that has not been cleaned in years — hot exhaust and fine lint escaping into the wall space and piling up around a machine that runs hot by design. The dryer overheats trying to push air through a blocked run, and the lint packed around it is exactly the fuel a fire needs.

That is why our cleaning checks the connection behind the dryer as well as the run itself — and why a disconnected or damaged line gets flagged, not ignored. Repairs are part of our related services.

Reduce the risk, step by step

Clean the full run yearly

The trap only catches part of the lint. The rest collects in the duct, which is why a full-run cleaning once a year is the standard recommendation.

Empty the trap every load

A clean trap improves airflow and keeps more lint out of the duct between professional cleanings.

Watch for warning signs

Longer drying times, a hot laundry room, or a burning smell are your vent asking for attention. See the six warning signs.

Our cleaning clears the full run from the dryer to the outside cap — $149 for first-floor laundry, $249 for second-floor laundry — and we flag crushed or disconnected ducts when we find them. We guarantee clean airflow with every cleaning.

When a cleaning isn’t the whole job.

Cleaning fixes a clogged vent. It does not fix a vent that is crushed, disconnected, routed the wrong way, or wide open to birds. These are the vent services that go with our cleaning — for homes, buildings, and rental portfolios across Broward County.

How pricing works: A standard cleaning is a flat $149 for 1st-floor laundry and $249 for 2nd-floor laundry. Every service below is priced by quote — we look at the vent run first and give you one price before any work starts.

Vent services beyond cleaning

Dryer Vent Repair

Vent lines get crushed when a dryer is pushed back, and connections work loose over time — a disconnected line dumps hot, lint-filled air into your wall or laundry room instead of outside. We reconnect loose joints and repair or replace crushed and damaged sections so the full run is sealed and flowing again.

Priced by quote

Vent Rerouting & Replacement

Some vents were installed the hard way: too long, too many sharp turns, or run in flimsy foil or plastic flex duct that traps lint in every ridge. We reroute problem runs the shorter, straighter way and replace unsafe duct with smooth rigid metal duct — the material dryer manufacturers recommend.

Priced by quote

Exterior Vent Cover & Bird Guard Installation

An open or broken exterior cap is an invitation — birds nest in warm vent runs and pests move in, blocking airflow from the outside in. We fit new vent covers and bird guards that let exhaust out freely while keeping animals out, and clear any nesting material already inside.

Priced by quote

Booster Fan Installation

The longer the vent run, the harder your dryer has to push — and on long runs, lint settles in the middle instead of making it out. A booster fan gives the exhaust the push it needs to clear the full distance, a common fix for interior laundry rooms and second-floor setups.

Priced by quote

Open to air. Closed to everything else.

A good exterior cover is a balance: the flap or grille has to open fully under exhaust pressure so your dryer can breathe, and close tight the rest of the time so birds, lizards, and wasps cannot move in. If your outside cap hangs open, is cracked, or has a nest behind it, replacing it is a small job that prevents a clogged — or occupied — vent run.

  • Covers and guards sized to your existing vent opening
  • Nesting material and lint cleared from the opening during the install
  • Airflow checked at the cap before we leave
